tagline: The big Gulf island — Chaweng and Lamai beaches, the Big Buddha, Hin Ta Hin Yai rocks, Bophut fishing village, and Ang Thong
introHtml:
Koh Samui is one of the largest islands in the Gulf of Thailand, off Surat Thani. It's an easy-to-reach holiday island with its own airport, white-sand beaches, resorts at every price point, and no shortage of places to eat and things to do. Most people picture Samui as Chaweng — the long, busy beach that buzzes day and night — and Lamai, which is a little quieter.

Beyond the beaches, Samui has the landmark Big Buddha at Wat Phra Yai, the Hin Ta Hin Yai rocks at Lamai, Wat Khunaram with the mummified body of Luang Pho Daeng, the Na Muang waterfalls in the middle of the island, and Bophut fishing village, which has turned into a seaside strip for eating and shopping. If you want to take a boat out snorkelling, Ang Thong Marine Park is one of the prettier day trips. Samui works for beach-goers, party people, families, and honeymooners alike.
bestTime: December–August, clear seas and good sun — great for swimming, snorkelling, and boat trips to Ang Thong · October–December is the Gulf monsoon, with heavy rain and rough surf

highlights.name: Chaweng Beach
highlights.blurb: Samui's longest and liveliest white-sand beach, packed with resorts, restaurants, beach clubs, and nightlife. It's the island's hub for accommodation and entertainment.

highlights.name: Lamai Beach
highlights.blurb: The second-biggest beach after Chaweng, quieter and more family-oriented. The Lamai night market and the Hin Ta Hin Yai rocks are both nearby.

highlights.name: Big Buddha (Wat Phra Yai)
highlights.blurb: A large golden Buddha image on Koh Fan, off the Bophut coast — a landmark you can spot from a distance. Climb the steps to pay respects and take in the sea view.

highlights.name: Hin Ta Hin Yai
highlights.blurb: A cluster of oddly shaped rocks by Lamai Beach that became a well-known photo spot. There's a local grandfather-and-grandmother legend behind it and a walkway along the rocks to watch the waves.

highlights.name: Bophut Fishing Village
highlights.blurb: The old seaside quarter at Bophut, with old wooden buildings, beachfront restaurants, cafes, and an evening market for eating and shopping. The vibe is more laid-back than Chaweng.

highlights.name: Ang Thong Marine Park
highlights.blurb: A chain of limestone islands in the Gulf, reached by boat from Samui, where you can snorkel, kayak, and climb to viewpoints over emerald-green water. It's one of the more scenic sea trips around.

foodScene.name: Fresh seafood
foodScene.note: As a fishing island, Samui has fresh prawns, shellfish, crab, and fish. Seafood places along the beaches and at Bophut village grill, steam, and stir-fry them with curry powder or in tom yum — eaten right by the water.

foodScene.name: Beachfront spots and beach clubs
foodScene.note: Chaweng, Lamai, and Bophut have beach clubs and seaside spots where you can eat and drink while watching the sunset — exactly the island feeling people come to Samui for.

foodScene.name: Lamai and Chaweng night markets
foodScene.note: The night markets around Lamai and Chaweng bring together Thai street food, grilled and fried snacks, and casual bites at friendlier prices than the resort restaurants.

foodScene.name: Bold southern Thai food
foodScene.note: Gaeng tai pla, gaeng lueang, khua kling, and khao yam turn up at local spots on the island — punchy southern flavours served with hot steamed rice.

foodScene.name: Cafes and brunch
foodScene.note: Samui has plenty of coffee shops, brunch places, and healthy eateries spread across Bophut, Chaweng, and Fisherman's Village — sit by the sea or out in a garden.

foodScene.name: International restaurants
foodScene.note: With lots of foreign visitors, Samui has solid Italian, French, Indian, and Mediterranean restaurants, especially around Chaweng and Fisherman's Village.

foodScene.name: Healthy and vegan food
foodScene.note: The island has plenty of vegan spots, smoothie bowls, and clean eating to suit the wellness and detox crowd staying long-term.

foodScene.name: Coconut sweets
foodScene.note: Samui is known for its coconuts, so you'll find coconut desserts, coconut ice cream, and fresh coconut water to cool off with throughout the day all over the island.

attractions.name: Chaweng Beach
attractions.blurb: Samui's longest and liveliest white-sand beach and the hub for accommodation, restaurants, beach clubs, and nightlife. Swimming and water activities are all here.

attractions.name: Lamai Beach
attractions.blurb: The second-biggest beach, quieter and more family-friendly, with the Lamai night market and the Hin Ta Hin Yai rocks nearby. Good for an unhurried break.

attractions.name: Big Buddha, Wat Phra Yai
attractions.blurb: A large golden Buddha image on Koh Fan off the Bophut coast — a landmark visible from a distance. Climb up to pay respects and take in the sea view.

attractions.name: Hin Ta Hin Yai
attractions.blurb: A cluster of oddly shaped rocks by Lamai Beach, a well-known photo spot with a grandfather-and-grandmother legend. Walk the rocks to watch the waves and the sunset.

attractions.name: Wat Khunaram (body of Luang Pho Daeng)
attractions.blurb: The temple that enshrines the mummified body of Luang Pho Daeng, seated in meditation. It's a place to pay respects and learn about the islanders' faith.

attractions.name: Na Muang Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A multi-tiered waterfall in the middle of the island with clear, cool water, swimming spots, and nearby elephant and ATV activities — a good stop to cool off.

attractions.name: Bophut Fishing Village
attractions.blurb: The old seaside quarter at Bophut, with old wooden buildings, beachfront restaurants, cafes, and an evening food market — a laid-back vibe by the sea.

attractions.name: Ang Thong Marine Park
attractions.blurb: A chain of limestone islands in the Gulf, reached by boat from Samui, for snorkelling, kayaking, and viewpoints over emerald-green water — one of the more scenic sea trips.
